facts.fact: The Minister for Finance told Parliament on 14 February 2020 that in the 2020/21 financial year government would extend its networks to the Tinkhundla Service Centres and health facilities and further digitalise its services; an intention announced in the budget speech, with no count of centres, cost or completion date.
facts.system: Extension of government networks to Tinkhundla Service Centres

facts.fact: The 2020 budget speech says the extension of government networks to the Tinkhundla Service Centres in 2020/21 would be done 'with the assistance of development partners'; it names no partner and no domestic budget line for it.
facts.system: Extension of government networks to Tinkhundla Service Centres

facts.fact: The 2020 budget speech presents the extension of networks to the Tinkhundla Service Centres as central government's own work, following its replacement of the government core network equipment.
facts.system: Extension of government networks to Tinkhundla Service Centres

note: The passages file holds no passage (the speech carries no study term); paragraph 94 was read in the mirror's whole copy, lines 966-989. The speech announces the connection and reports none made: no centre is said to be on the network, so no `connected`, `use` or `authorities` fact is taken. The Regional Development Fund's rise from E110 million to E177 million for the Tinkhundla is not an ICT line.
